youtube.title: Why Is the US Town of Point Roberts Trapped by Canada?
youtube.description:
Point Roberts, Washington is a US town of about 1,200 people that you can only drive to through Canada. Older students cross an international border four times a day just to get to school and back. How did a piece of America end up cut off like this?

On the map, we follow the straight line drawn in 1846, the surveyors and settlers who came after it, how the town lives today between two countries, what the 2020 border closure and the 2025 trade dispute did to it, and three ways its map could still change.

{CHAPTERS}

youtube.comment: If you lived in Point Roberts, would you want a ferry, a Canadian flag, or nothing changed? 👇

sources.claim: Point Roberts covers about 12.7 square kilometres of land
sources.source: US Census Bureau, Point Roberts CDP land area (4.89 sq mi), 2020 Census Gazetteer

sources.claim: About 1,200 people live in Point Roberts
sources.source: US Census Bureau, 2020 Census, Point Roberts CDP (1,191)

sources.claim: Older students are bused to schools in Blaine, crossing the border four times a day
sources.source: Blaine School District (Point Roberts Primary serves the youngest grades); reported by CBC News and The Seattle Times, 2020-2021

sources.claim: Older pupils go to middle and high school in Blaine
sources.source: Blaine School District, school listings (Blaine Middle School, Blaine High School)

sources.claim: The road trip to Blaine through Canada is about 40 kilometres
sources.source: Whatcom County, Point Roberts transportation information; route measured on Google Maps, 2026

sources.claim: The 49th parallel forms the border for about 2,000 kilometres west of Lake of the Woods
sources.source: International Boundary Commission; Convention of 1818 and Oregon Treaty 1846

sources.claim: Its only land border is about five kilometres long
sources.source: Measured along 49°N from Monument Park (123.092°W) to the Boundary Bay shore (123.025°W), about 4.9 km; International Boundary Commission boundary data

sources.claim: Point Roberts tap water has been supplied by Greater Vancouver since the late 1980s
sources.source: Point Roberts Water District; Greater Vancouver Water District supply agreement, 1987

sources.claim: Electricity reaches Point Roberts through Canadian lines, sold by an American utility
sources.source: Puget Sound Energy, Point Roberts service information

sources.claim: Spanish sailors in 1791 charted the peninsula as an island
sources.source: HistoryLink.org, 'Point Roberts — Thumbnail History' (Narváez expedition, 'Isla de Zepeda')

sources.claim: George Vancouver named Point Roberts in 1792 after Henry Roberts
sources.source: George Vancouver, A Voyage of Discovery to the North Pacific Ocean (1798); HistoryLink.org

sources.claim: Britain and the US both claimed the Oregon Country, from today's California-Oregon line (42°N) north to Russian Alaska at 54°40'
sources.source: US Department of State, Office of the Historian, 'The Oregon Territory, 1846'; Adams-Onís Treaty 1819 (42°N); Russo-American Treaty 1824 and Anglo-Russian Treaty 1825 (54°40'N)

sources.claim: The 1818 treaty set the 49th parallel east of the Rockies and left the west open to both for ten years
sources.source: Convention of 1818, Articles II and III, 20 October 1818

sources.claim: Renewed in 1827, the shared arrangement lasted almost thirty years
sources.source: Convention of 6 August 1827 (joint occupation extended indefinitely); ended by the Oregon Treaty, 15 June 1846: 1818-1846 is 28 years

sources.claim: Polk called the US claim to Oregon 'clear and unquestionable'
sources.source: James K. Polk, Inaugural Address, 4 March 1845

sources.claim: Britain wanted the line along the Columbia River
sources.source: US Department of State, Office of the Historian, 'The Oregon Territory, 1846'

sources.claim: The gap between the two claims was more than 900 kilometres
sources.source: Measured: 54°40'N (US claim) to the Columbia River mouth, about 46°15'N

sources.claim: The Oregon Treaty of June 1846 extended the 49th parallel to the sea and kept Vancouver Island British
sources.source: Oregon Treaty, signed 15 June 1846, Article I

sources.claim: Historians generally think the negotiators overlooked the peninsula
sources.source: HistoryLink.org, 'Point Roberts — Thumbnail History'

sources.claim: British officials suggested the US give up the tip; Washington did not agree
sources.source: HistoryLink.org, 'Point Roberts — Thumbnail History'

sources.claim: In 1859 the US made the tip a military reserve; no fort was built; opened to settlers in 1908
sources.source: HistoryLink.org, 'Point Roberts — Thumbnail History'

sources.claim: Joint survey from 1857; granite boundary marker set at Point Roberts in 1861
sources.source: Northwest Boundary Survey records, 1857-1861; International Boundary Commission

sources.claim: Icelandic families settled in the 1890s; canneries and fish traps in the early 1900s
sources.source: HistoryLink.org; Point Roberts Historical Society

sources.claim: The Tsawwassen ferry terminal opened in 1960
sources.source: BC Ferries corporate history

sources.claim: Canadians bought summer cabins on the American side and the town grew around them
sources.source: HistoryLink.org, 'Point Roberts — Thumbnail History' (post-war Canadian summer residents)

sources.claim: In 1971 the two governments asked the International Joint Commission to study Point Roberts; ideas included a shared international park
sources.source: International Joint Commission, Point Roberts Reference (1971) and report to governments (1970s)

sources.claim: Local officials say most property owners are Canadian
sources.source: CBC News, Point Roberts reporting, 2020 and 2025

sources.claim: Canadians rent US mailboxes in Point Roberts for online orders
sources.source: CBC News; The New York Times, Point Roberts reporting, 2025

sources.claim: Canadians cross for fuel and groceries at the town's shops
sources.source: CBC News, Point Roberts business reporting, 2020 and 2025

sources.claim: Downtown Vancouver lies about 30 kilometres north of the border gate in a straight line
sources.source: Measured straight line, Point Roberts crossing (49.002°N, 123.068°W) to downtown Vancouver (49.282°N, 123.120°W), about 31 km; road distance is longer

sources.claim: Metro Vancouver had about 2.6 million people in 2021
sources.source: Statistics Canada, 2021 Census, Vancouver CMA (2,642,825)

sources.claim: The Point Roberts crossing is open every hour of every day
sources.source: US Customs and Border Protection; Canada Border Services Agency port listings

sources.claim: The land border closed to non-essential travel on 21 March 2020
sources.source: Joint US-Canada announcement, March 2020; Federal Register, 24 March 2020

sources.claim: Whatcom County ran a small passenger boat to Bellingham during the closure
sources.source: Whatcom County, Point Roberts passenger ferry pilot, 2020-2021

sources.claim: Point Roberts was cut off from most Canadian visitors for almost twenty months
sources.source: Counted from the closure on 21 March 2020 to the US land border reopening on 8 November 2021 (about 19.5 months)

sources.claim: Canada reopened to vaccinated Americans on 9 August 2021; the US land border reopened 8 November 2021
sources.source: Government of Canada, July 2021; US Department of Homeland Security, October 2021

sources.claim: Canadian return car trips from the US fell about 35% in April 2025
sources.source: Statistics Canada, Leading indicator of international arrivals, April 2025 (-35.2% year over year)

sources.claim: Many Canadians said they stayed home in response to US tariffs and annexation talk
sources.source: Statistics Canada travel data and Leger polling, 2025

sources.claim: The US government said its tariffs were about border security, drugs and American jobs
sources.source: White House fact sheet, 1 February 2025

sources.claim: NEXUS cards speed up crossings for pre-approved travellers
sources.source: US Customs and Border Protection; Canada Border Services Agency, NEXUS program

sources.claim: Point Roberts is part of Whatcom County; residents vote in US elections and attend US schools
sources.source: Whatcom County Auditor, elections precincts; Blaine School District

sources.claim: 180 years since the line was drawn
sources.source: Oregon Treaty, 1846; counted to 2026

sources.claim: In that time, the town lived through two world wars, a long border closure and a trade dispute
sources.source: World War I (1914-1918) and World War II (1939-1945), Encyclopaedia Britannica; border closure 2020-2021 and 2025 tariff dispute as sourced above

sources.claim: Minnesota's Northwest Angle lies north of the 49th parallel at Lake of the Woods and is reached by road only through Canada
sources.source: Minnesota Department of Natural Resources; Lake of the Woods County; International Boundary Commission
